# Vendored: dyad-sh/dyad at 00d5f5af7fd0 (v1.15.0-beta.1, 2026-09-10)

Taken with `git archive` from the pinned commit: src, scaffold, worker, shared, packages, index.html,
package.json, package-lock.json, vite.renderer.config.mts, tsconfig*.json, components.json, LICENSE,
NOTICE, README.md, AGENTS.md.

Removed: `src/pro/` (Functional Source License 1.1; not reused). Everything kept is Apache 2.0 per
LICENSE.

Changes to reused files are listed here, one line each, so upstream can be tracked:

- `hologram.contracts.ts` (ours) also publishes imported input schemas as `window.__inputContracts`; the browser host validates and copies command inputs before effects, and returns typed refusals rather than synthesizing successful output.

- `src/pro/` is not Dyad's: four small files of ours export the names the renderer imports from the
  removed folder, so the renderer builds without the Functional Source License code:
  `shared/search_replace_parser.ts` (a parser for the SEARCH / REPLACE blocks the chat renders),
  `ui/components/Annotator/Annotator.tsx` (hands the screenshot back as one attachment; no drawing),
  `main/ipc/handlers/local_agent/tool_definitions.ts` (the tool name type; the names are the PrismPM tool contract's),
  `main/prompts/turbo_edits_v2_prompt.ts` (empty; turbo edits are a Pro feature and not offered).
- `scaffold/src/App.tsx`, as staged for the shell only (the vendored file is untouched): `<BrowserRouter basename={import.meta.env.BASE_URL}>`, so a project routes correctly when served under its address path instead of an origin root.
- `src/router.ts`: `basepath: import.meta.env.BASE_URL.replace(/\/$/, "")` on `createRouter`, so Dyad's routes live under the base the shell is served from (`/app/` locally, `/dyad-prism/app/` on Pages) and a refresh finds them.
- `src/components/preview_panel/PublishPanel.tsx`: one import and one mount of `HologramSection` (ours, `src/components/preview_panel/HologramSection.tsx`) above Dyad's deployment section, so the Publish panel offers "Publish as a Hologram application": the host composes a `.holo` v4 through PrismPM's own archive code in the core and serves it under its address. The words are the View's. For an app with rules the button says "publish" in the app's chat instead (through `useStreamChat`, as Dyad's Refactor button does), and the host builds the app with the Prism SDK on GitHub Actions (`shell/host.js` publishTurn).
- `vite.shell.config.mts` (ours, added): the vendored Vite config plus fixed output names, so the shell's projected homepage can reference `assets/index.js` and `assets/index.css`; the renderer is now the homepage at the shell's root, the `--base` is the shell's base.
- The product's name: `vite.shell.config.mts` replaces every standalone `Dyad` word in `src/**` (sources, locales, markdown) with `Hologram` at build time and resolves `assets/logo.svg` to Hologram's mark; identifiers (`DyadError`, `dyad-write`, `__dyadIpcEnvelope`) are untouched. The vendored files themselves keep Dyad's words. `scripts/stamp_shell.py` does the same for the staged scaffold (the badge reads "Made with Hologram" and links to gethologram.ai).
- Three controls removed at build (`vite.shell.config.mts`): the setup pill under the home composer ("Manage AI setup" / "Connect AI to build", `src/pages/home.tsx`, its condition becomes `false`), the Pro selector (`src/components/ChatInputControls.tsx`, `<ProModeSelector />` becomes `{null}`); and the voice to text button (Dyad's Pro feature) is hidden by `shell/appearance.css` through its labels. The vendored files are untouched.
- `src/components/ModelPicker.tsx` is replaced at build by ours (`vendor/dyad/hologram.ModelPicker.tsx`, aliased in `vite.shell.config.mts`): two models, GLM 5.3 Flash (Cloud) and BitNet 2B (Local), each tagged with where it runs. Dyad's picker carries an "All models" submenu, a recent section, per model effort levels, price badges, a trial banner, local provider submenus for Ollama and LM Studio, and an "Unlock all models with Pro" row; none of those apply here. Ours writes what Dyad's wrote, the settings record's `selectedModel` and the chat's own selection once the chat has a history, so every screen stays in sync.
- `src/components/ChatInputControls.tsx`: the chat mode selector is removed at build (`<ChatModeSelector />` becomes `{null}`) and the host keeps the record's mode on build. This host implements one mode, Dyad's text tag build turn; its agent and plan modes promise tool calls that are not made here, and the composer showed "Basic Agent" while a build turn ran.
- `src/components/chat/ChatInput.tsx`: the promo row under the composer is not rendered (`{showPromo && <PromoMessage seed={promo.seed} />}` becomes `{null}`). Its messages sell Dyad Pro and point at Dyad's GitHub, subreddit and X account; the word transform would put Hologram's name on all of it.
- `src/renderer.tsx`: one import is prepended at build, `vendor/dyad/hologram.contracts.ts` (ours), which publishes every contract's output schema on the page as `window.__contracts`. Dyad's renderer types its calls but validates nothing it receives, so a host answer of the wrong shape used to reach a screen and crash it far from the cause; `shell/host.js` now parses every answer against the channel's own contract.
- The ui components are shadcn/ui new-york-v4 as the Hologram brand kit vendors it, not Dyad's (`hologram.ui.mjs`, ours, used by `vite.shell.config.mts`): every import of a name the kit has (`@/components/ui/button`, or a relative `./ui/button`) resolves to the kit's file under `vendor/shadcn-ui/registry/new-york-v4/` (written by `tools/live_components.mjs --vendor`, digests in `vendor/shadcn-ui/VENDORED.sha256`), and the build refuses a bundle that holds Base UI or Dyad's copy of a kit component. Dyad's own `src/components/ui/*` are untouched and never shipped; its five components the kit does not have (`ColorPicker`, `LoadingBar`, `NumberInput`, `SimpleAvatar`, `back-button`) are kept and are built from the kit's. Tailwind scans the kit's directory (`@source`, added to `globals.css` at build).
- Every screen's calls to those components are rewritten at build from Base UI's props to Radix's (`hologram.radix.mjs`, ours): `render={<El/>}` and `as` become `asChild`, Accordion and ToggleGroup take `type`, `TooltipProvider delay` is `delayDuration`, `closeOnClick={false}` is `onSelect` preventing default, `keepMounted` is `forceMount`, a `SelectValue` render function is called with its Select's value, `MiniSelectTrigger` is the kit's `SelectTrigger` at `size="sm"`, a `CommandDialog` filter goes on a cmdk `Command` inside it, a relative ui import names `@/components/ui/`. The vendored files are untouched. `hologram.typecheck.mjs` (ours, with `tsconfig.hologram.json` and `tsconfig.hologram.dyad.json`) typechecks the rewritten screens against the kit's components and refuses an error Dyad's own sources do not have, or a call the rewrite could not convert.
- The shell's own screens, after shadcn's dashboard-01 block and built only from the kit's components, through `hologram.screens.mjs` (ours, applied by `vite.shell.config.mts` and by the typecheck): `src/components/app-sidebar.tsx` is replaced whole by `hologram.screens/AppSidebar.tsx` (an inset sidebar that collapses to icons: Prism's mark, a triangle of three faces drawn in the text colour, and the name "Prism AI Foundry", New app, Home, Apps, Templates, Library, Plugins, the user's apps with the open app's chats, Settings and Help, plus the site header), and `src/pages/apps.tsx` by `hologram.screens/AppsPage.tsx` (section cards with trend badges from the apps' and chats' own dates, tabs with counts, a data table with row selection, a row menu and Dyad's bulk delete, and Dyad's collection views and dialogs). `src/components/ui/back-button.tsx` is replaced by `hologram.screens/BackButton.tsx`, which draws nothing: the site header carries a breadcrumb (the kit's Breadcrumb) to the page above. Each is compiled at the path of the file it replaces. Patches, each refusing the build if its passage is gone (a retag patch renames one element and its closing tag, found by the TypeScript parser): `src/pages/settings.tsx` draws each settings section as the kit's Card and drops its own title (the header names the page); `src/pages/plugins.tsx`, `src/pages/templates.tsx` and `src/pages/library-home.tsx` take the inset's page spacing and keep their description and actions without a second title; `src/pages/app-details.tsx` sits on the kit's Card instead of a box styled as one, and shows its dates as dates; `src/app/layout.tsx` puts the page in the sidebar's `SidebarInset` under the site header and opens the sidebar by default; `src/components/ZoomSelector.tsx` names the chosen level's label alone in the trigger (Radix shows the chosen item whole, description included). `hologram.env.d.ts` (ours) types an imported `.svg` for the typecheck.
- `src/pages/chat.tsx`, through `hologram.screens.mjs`: on a phone (the kit's `useIsMobile`, the sidebar's own 768 px breakpoint) the build screen returns `hologram.screens/MobileBuild.tsx` (ours, kit components only) instead of the two resizable panels: one pane at a time (chat, or the preview panel in its preview or publish mode, both kept mounted) and a bottom bar with back to the apps and Chat / Preview / Publish as the kit's `Tabs`. Two patches: one import line, and `const isMobile = useIsMobile(); if (isMobile) return <MobileBuild ... />;` before the `PanelGroup`. Wider screens are unchanged.
- `package.json`, `package-lock.json`: `radix-ui` 1.6.7 added, exactly as the brand kit's showcase pins it (the kit's components import it); npm moved the `@radix-ui/*` packages Dyad already had through `cmdk` and `vaul` to the versions it requires, and `react-remove-scroll` from 2.7.1 to 2.7.2.
- `hologram.GitHubIntegration.tsx` (ours) replaces `src/components/GitHubIntegration.tsx` at build time through `resolveId` in `vite.shell.config.mts`: Settings → Integrations → GitHub takes a pasted token (checked once against api.github.com), because GitHub's device flow is not served to web pages. Publishing uses it to build apps with the Prism SDK.
- `hologram.ImportAppDialog.tsx` (ours) replaces `src/components/ImportAppDialog.tsx` at build time through `resolveId` in `vite.shell.config.mts` (its one user is `ImportAppButton.tsx`; `AI_RULES_PROMPT` is still exported): Import App on the home page takes a Forge export file (`hologram-forge/export/1`, written by the moved page of the site Forge was served from before) and the host's `forge:import` writes its apps, chats, files and versions under new ids. Dyad's dialog imports a folder from disk or a GitHub repository, neither of which a web page has. The file never carries settings or keys.
